topics.name: Speaking and Listening
objectives: Listen and respond appropriately to adults and their peers
Ask relevant questions to extend their understanding
Use relevant strategies to build vocabulary
Articulate and justify answers, arguments and opinions
Describe events or experiences giving well-structured descriptions
Maintain attention and participate actively in collaborative conversations

keyVocab.definition: The people who are listening
The person talking
Talk about something with others, sharing ideas
What you think or believe about something
An explanation for why you think something

masteryIndicators: I can listen carefully and respond to what others say
I can ask a question to find out more
I can explain my ideas in full sentences
I can take turns in a group discussion
topics.starter: Show and Tell: one pupil describes an object from a bag using adjectives; class asks one question each
topics.guidedPractice: Think-Pair-Share: teacher poses a question, pupils discuss in pairs, then share with the class using 'We think… because…'
topics.independentPractice: Developing: answer with a word or phrase. Expected: answer in a full sentence with a reason. Mastery: ask a follow-up question and justify their view.
topics.masteryCheck: Give pupils a simple scenario — each explains what they would do and why, using a full sentence.

topics.name: Phonics – Decoding
objectives: Apply phonic knowledge and skills as the route to decode words
Respond speedily with the correct sound to graphemes for all 40+ phonemes
Read accurately by blending sounds in unfamiliar words
Read common exception words
Read words containing taught GPCs and common suffixes
Read aloud accurately books that are consistent with their phonic knowledge

keyVocab.definition: The smallest unit of sound in a word
The written letter(s) that represent a phoneme
Grapheme-Phoneme Correspondence — the link between a written letter and its sound
To push sounds together to read a word
To split a word into individual sounds to spell it
Two letters that make one sound, e.g. 'sh', 'ch'
A word that cannot easily be decoded phonically and must be learned by sight (e.g. 'said', 'the')

masteryIndicators: I can quickly read all Phase 5 graphemes
I can blend to read unfamiliar words accurately
I can read at least 45 common exception words
I can read aloud with increasing fluency
topics.starter: Flashcard speed round: show grapheme cards, pupils call the sound
topics.guidedPractice: Shared reading: teacher models blending for an unfamiliar word in context, then pupils try with partner support
topics.independentPractice: Developing: read simple CVC words. Expected: blend Phase 5 graphemes. Mastery: read unfamiliar multi-syllabic words and self-correct.
topics.masteryCheck: Read 10 words containing the target grapheme. Read 5 common exception words from the Year 1 list.

topics.name: Fluency and Comprehension
objectives: Continue to apply phonic knowledge until automatic decoding has become embedded
Read accurately whole words, including common exception words
Read most words quickly and accurately without sounding out loud
Read aloud books closely matched to improving reading level with confidence
Read words with common suffixes

keyVocab.definition: Reading smoothly, at a good pace, with expression
Reading each word correctly
Using your voice to show meaning — changing pace, tone and volume
Letters added to the end of a word to change its meaning, e.g. -ment, -ness, -ful

masteryIndicators: I can read Year 2 common exception words fluently
I can read aloud with expression and appropriate pace
I can decode unfamiliar words quickly
I can self-correct when my reading doesn't make sense
topics.starter: Paired reading: pupils read aloud to each other from a familiar text
topics.guidedPractice: Echo reading: teacher reads a sentence with expression, pupils repeat matching the expression
topics.independentPractice: Developing: read from levelled text aloud. Expected: read with pace and accuracy. Mastery: read with expression, changing pace/tone for effect.
topics.masteryCheck: Read a short passage aloud. Assess: accuracy, pace, expression. Can the pupil self-correct errors?

topics.name: Reading Comprehension
objectives: Develop pleasure in reading, motivation to read, vocabulary and understanding
Understand both the books they can already read accurately and those they listen to
Explain clearly their understanding of what is read to them
Make inferences on the basis of what is being said and done
Predict what might happen on the basis of what has been read so far
Discuss the significance of the title and events
Make links between the book they are reading and other books they have read
Recognise and discuss simple recurring literary language

keyVocab.definition: Find an answer that is directly in the text
Work out something that is not directly stated using clues in the text
Use clues to say what might happen next
Retell only the most important parts
The words used in a text
A made-up story
A text about real people, places or events

masteryIndicators: I can retrieve information directly from the text
I can make a simple inference supported by evidence
I can predict what will happen next and give a reason
I can discuss the meaning of unfamiliar words using context
topics.starter: Book talk: show the cover — what do you predict? What clues helped you?
topics.guidedPractice: Shared text: teacher reads, pauses to ask 'How do you know?', 'What does this word mean here?'; pupils answer with evidence
topics.independentPractice: Developing: one retrieval question (answer in text). Expected: one inference question with evidence. Mastery: explain how the author chose language to create effect.
topics.masteryCheck: Read the passage and answer: one retrieval, one inference, and one vocabulary question.

topics.name: Spelling
objectives: Spell words containing each of the 40+ phonemes already taught
Spell common exception words for Years 1 and 2
Spell words with common suffixes: -s, -es, -ing, -ed, -er, -est
Add prefixes and suffixes: un-, -ful, -less, -ness, -ment
Apply simple spelling rules and guidance
Write from memory simple sentences dictated by the teacher

keyVocab.definition: Letters added to the start of a word to change its meaning, e.g. un-, dis-
Letters added to the end of a word to change its meaning, e.g. -ful, -ness
The base word before a prefix or suffix is added
When a consonant is repeated before adding -ed or -ing, e.g. running
A beat or chunk within a word, e.g. hap-py has 2 syllables

masteryIndicators: I can spell all Year 1 and Year 2 common exception words
I can add -ful, -less, -ness, -ment correctly
I can apply the doubling rule (running, hopping)
I can write dictated sentences accurately
topics.starter: Look-cover-write-check with 5 words from the Year list
topics.guidedPractice: Investigate the suffix -ful: add to care, hope, help — notice the spelling pattern
topics.independentPractice: Developing: add suffix to given words. Expected: apply suffix rules in sentences. Mastery: investigate a new suffix and write their own examples.
topics.masteryCheck: Dictation: teacher reads 3 sentences using the target spelling pattern. Pupils write and self-mark.

topics.name: Handwriting
objectives: Sit correctly at a table, holding a pencil comfortably
Form lower-case letters in the correct direction, starting and finishing in the right place
Form capital letters and digits
Form lower-case letters of the correct size relative to each other
Begin to use some of the diagonal and horizontal strokes needed to join letters

keyVocab.definition: The part of a letter that rises above the x-height, e.g. b, d, h
The part of a letter that falls below the baseline, e.g. g, p, y
The correct starting point and direction for writing each letter
A stroke connecting one letter to the next

masteryIndicators: I can form all lowercase letters correctly from the right starting point
I can form capital letters correctly
I can write letters consistently sized
I can begin joining letters using diagonal strokes
topics.starter: Finger trace on partner's back — can they guess the letter?
topics.guidedPractice: Teacher models formation of letters in the target family on the board; pupils practise on whiteboards
topics.independentPractice: Developing: trace over dotted letters. Expected: copy letters independently. Mastery: form target letters in joined writing in sentences.
topics.masteryCheck: Write a sentence using the target letter family in best handwriting. Check: correct formation, size, spacing.

topics.name: Narrative Writing
objectives: Write sentences that can be read by themselves and others
Demarcate some sentences with capital letters and full stops
Use coordination (using or, and, but) and subordination (using when, if, that, because)
Sequence sentences to form short narratives
Re-read to check that their writing makes sense
Write about real events, recording these simply and clearly
Use the punctuation taught so far consistently

keyVocab.definition: A group of words that makes complete sense, starting with a capital letter and ending with punctuation
A word that joins two clauses, e.g. and, but, because, when, if
A word that describes a noun
A word that adds detail to a verb
A naming word — a person, place or thing
A doing or being word
An uppercase letter used to begin a sentence or a proper noun

masteryIndicators: I can write a sentence that makes sense, with a capital letter and full stop
I can use 'because', 'and', 'but' to extend my sentences
I can sequence at least 3 sentences to tell a story
I can re-read my writing to check it makes sense
topics.starter: Sentence or not? Teacher reads aloud — pupils show thumbs up/down if it is a complete sentence
topics.guidedPractice: Shared writing: class creates a story opening together using a picture stimulus; teacher models thinking aloud, checking sentences
topics.independentPractice: Developing: write one sentence about a picture. Expected: write 3+ linked sentences to start a story. Mastery: vary sentences using conjunctions; include adjectives for effect.
topics.masteryCheck: Write 3 sentences to continue the story. Check: capital letters, full stops, use of conjunction.

topics.name: Non-fiction Writing
objectives: Write about real events, recording these simply and clearly
Write for different purposes including writing under different headings
Use features of non-fiction texts: headings, labels, captions, questions
Discuss what they have written with the teacher or other pupils

keyVocab.definition: A title for a section of writing
A smaller title within a section
A sentence explaining a picture or diagram
Something that is true and can be checked
The reason a text was written (to inform, instruct, persuade)
Who the writing is for

masteryIndicators: I can write facts in full sentences
I can use headings to organise my writing
I can write for a specific audience and purpose
I can include at least one non-fiction text feature
topics.starter: Show two texts (fiction vs non-fiction) — how can you tell? What features give it away?
topics.guidedPractice: Shared write: create a fact file about an animal together — teacher models headings, caption, bullet-point facts
topics.independentPractice: Developing: complete a fact file template with given information. Expected: write own fact file with headings. Mastery: choose own non-fiction form and justify features used.
topics.masteryCheck: Write a short information text about [topic] with at least two headings and three facts.

topics.name: Sentence Grammar
objectives: Leave spaces between words
Join words and clauses using 'and'
Begin to punctuate sentences using a capital letter and a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark
Use a capital letter for names of people, places, the days of the week, and the personal pronoun 'I'
Understand and use the following terminology: letter, capital letter, word, singular, plural, sentence, punctuation, full stop, question mark, exclamation mark
Subordination (using when, if, that, because) and coordination (using or, and, but)
Expanded noun phrases to describe and specify
Correct choice and consistent use of present tense and past tense
Use of the suffixes –ment, –ness, –ful, –less, –ly

keyVocab.definition: A noun and its describing words, e.g. 'the big red ball'
A noun phrase made longer with adjectives and/or prepositional phrases
A conjunction that joins a subordinate clause to a main clause, e.g. because, when, if, that
A conjunction that joins two equal clauses, e.g. and, but, or
Whether something is happening now (present) or happened before (past)
One person or thing
More than one person or thing

masteryIndicators: I can use capital letters and full stops correctly
I can use question marks and exclamation marks
I can write expanded noun phrases
I can use subordinating conjunctions to extend sentences
topics.starter: Punctuation surgeon: class corrects a paragraph with missing capital letters and full stops
topics.guidedPractice: Expanded noun phrase builder: start with 'the dog' → 'the fluffy, brown dog' → 'the fluffy, brown dog with a wagging tail'
topics.independentPractice: Developing: add capital letters and full stops to sentences. Expected: write expanded noun phrases in sentences. Mastery: write a paragraph using coordination and subordination.
topics.masteryCheck: Improve these sentences by adding expanded noun phrases and a conjunction: 'The cat sat. It was hungry.'
